rules.title: New York — Wage Notice at Hire

params.contents: rate(s) and basis; regular and overtime rates for non-exempt employees; payday; allowances; employer legal and DBA names, address, phone
params.language_requirement: English and the employee's identified primary language (DOL templates)
params.change_notice: at least 7 calendar days before the change unless shown on the wage statement
params.notes: Form LS 54 and variants; damages up to $5,000 per employee

result.summary: Employers must give each new hire a written notice (Wage Theft Prevention Act) of rate and basis of pay, overtime rate, payday, allowances and employer names and addresses in English and the employee's primary language, with a signed acknowledgment kept 6 years and 7 days' written notice of changes.

citations.source: Ezel, New-Hire Wage Notice Requirements by State (survey)

rules.title: New York City — Ban the Box

params.notes: Amended 2021-07-29 to cover pending arrests and current employees

result.summary: Employers of four or more may not ask about criminal history until after a conditional offer, must apply the Article 23-A factors in a written analysis and hold the position open at least 5 business days for the applicant's response.

citations.source: Accurate, Ban the Box Laws by Jurisdiction (survey)

rules.title: New York — Salary History Ban

result.summary: Employers may not rely on or seek an applicant's or employee's wage history; they may confirm history the applicant volunteers to support a higher offer.

citations.source: HR Dive, Salary history bans: a running list (survey)

rules.title: New York City — Salary History Ban

result.summary: Employers may not ask about an applicant's salary or benefits history or rely on it to set pay unless the applicant volunteers it.

citations.source: HR Dive, Salary history bans: a running list (survey)

rules.title: New York — Pay Range Disclosure

params.remote_coverage: roles performed outside NY that report to a NY supervisor, office or worksite

result.summary: Employers of four or more must include the compensation or range and the job description in postings for jobs, promotions or transfers performed in New York or reporting to a New York supervisor.

citations.source: Clockspot, Pay Transparency Laws by State (survey)

rules.title: New York City — Pay Range Disclosure

params.remote_coverage: any role that could be performed, in whole or part, in NYC including remote

result.summary: Employers of four or more must state the good-faith minimum and maximum salary in every advertisement for a job, promotion or transfer that could be performed in New York City.

citations.source: Clockspot, Pay Transparency Laws by State (survey)

rules.title: New York Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Employers with 10 or more employees pay the first $40 of the daily wage for the first 3 days of jury service

rules.title: New York Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 2 hours of paid leave at the start or end of the shift to vote, requested 2 to 10 working days ahead, unless the employee has 4 consecutive non-working hours while polls are open

citations.source: N.Y. Elec. Law §3-110 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: New York — Reasonable Accommodation for Domestic Violence Victims

params.covered_reasons: medical attention, victim services, counseling, safety planning or relocation, legal assistance and court proceedings

result.summary: Employers must provide reasonable accommodation, including a reasonable amount of time off, to an employee who is a victim of domestic violence for medical care, victim services, counseling, relocation or legal proceedings unless undue hardship; accrued paid leave may be charged first (Exec. Law 296(22)). Safe leave is also a use of NY paid sick leave (Labor Law 196-b).

rules.title: USERRA — Uniformed Services Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: uniformed services (active duty, reserve and National Guard federal duty, training)

result.summary: All employers must grant unpaid leave for service in the uniformed services and reemploy the employee in the escalator position after up to 5 cumulative years of service, with no discrimination or retaliation; health coverage continues up to 24 months at the employee's expense. State-ordered National Guard duty is covered only by state law.

rules.title: New York — State Military Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: state active duty and National Guard or state militia service

result.summary: Unpaid leave for state active duty, drills, training or service school with reinstatement unless unreasonable, or a position of like seniority, status and pay; discrimination barred. (Survey-based encoding; dates not researched.)

citations.source: Workplace Fairness, State Laws on Military Leave (50-state survey, used for encoding)

result.summary: Employers with 20 or more employees at one site must give an employee who works 20 or more hours a week up to 10 days of unpaid leave while a spouse on active duty in a combat theater or zone is on leave.

rules.title: Federal FMLA — Employee Eligibility

result.summary: Employee is FMLA-eligible: entitled to up to 12 weeks unpaid job-protected leave

rules.title: FLSA — Hours Worked Standard

params.notes: Hours worked = time the employee is suffered or permitted to work; the Portal-to-Portal Act excludes ordinary commuting and activities preliminary or postliminary to the principal activity (incl. security screening, Integrity Staffing v. Busk 2014); 29 CFR 785.47 lets insubstantial, irregular minutes be disregarded

result.summary: Under the FLSA all time an employee is suffered or permitted to work is paid, except ordinary commuting and preliminary or postliminary activities excluded by the Portal-to-Portal Act; a de minimis exception exists.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Commute)

result.summary: Ordinary home-to-work travel is not hours worked, even to different worksites, unless the employee works during the trip.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Between Worksites)

result.summary: Travel between job sites during the workday, or from the employer's premises to the first site after reporting, is hours worked.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Special One Day Assignment)

params.notes: Employer may deduct the normal home-to-work commute time

result.summary: A special one-day assignment in another city is hours worked, less the time of the employee's normal commute.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Out Of Town)

result.summary: Overnight travel away from home is hours worked only during the employee's normal working hours (including corresponding hours on non-working days); passenger time outside those hours is unpaid unless work is done.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Employer Mandated Transport)

result.summary: Riding employer-provided transport from a meeting point to the worksite is not hours worked under the Portal-to-Portal Act unless the travel is itself a principal activity; several states (CA, NY, WA, MD, PA, MA) count it.

rules.title: FLSA — Restricted On-Call Time

params.test: engaged to wait: employee must remain on the premises or so close that the time cannot be used effectively for personal purposes

result.summary: An employee required to stay on or near the premises while on call is working and must be paid.

rules.title: FLSA — Unrestricted On-Call Time

params.test: waiting to be engaged: employee may leave a contact number and use the time for personal purposes
params.notes: Time actually spent responding to calls is paid

result.summary: An on-call employee who need only leave a contact number and can use the time freely is not working; only time responding to calls is paid.

rules.title: FLSA — Mandatory Training and Meetings

params.notes: Attendance is not voluntary if required or if the employee is led to believe non-attendance would hurt their job

result.summary: Required training, orientation and meetings are hours worked.

rules.title: FLSA — Voluntary Training Outside Hours

params.exclusion_test: all four: outside regular hours, genuinely voluntary, not directly related to the employee's current job, and no productive work performed
params.notes: Training to acquire a new or additional skill is not 'directly related'; apprenticeship instruction and independent courses are excluded

result.summary: Training is unpaid only when it is outside regular hours, voluntary, not directly related to the current job and involves no productive work; otherwise it is hours worked.

rules.title: FLSA — Time Clock Rounding

params.notes: Rounding to the nearest 5, 6 or 15 minutes is accepted where it averages out and does not fail to pay for all time actually worked over a period

result.summary: Punches may be rounded to the nearest quarter hour (or smaller increment) if the practice is neutral and does not, over time, fail to pay employees for all hours worked.

rules.title: New York — Hours Worked Standard

result.summary: New York counts time the employee is required to be available for work at a place prescribed by the employer, which reaches mandatory pre-shift logistics and employer-required transit; the citation URL is a placeholder for the Labor Department regulation.

rules.title: New York — Travel Time (Employer Mandated Transport)

result.summary: Time an employee is required to be available for work at a place the employer prescribes, including mandatory transit from a reporting point, is hours worked.

rules.title: New York — Travel Time (Between Worksites)

result.summary: Travel between worksites during the workday is hours worked.

rules.title: New York — Time Clock Rounding

result.summary: The New York Labor Department follows the federal rounding regulation: neutral rounding to the nearest quarter hour is permitted.

rules.title: Federal Workweek Definition (FLSA)

result.summary: Overtime is computed over a fixed and regularly recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods) that may begin on any day and hour; it may be changed only permanently and not to evade overtime, and hours may not be averaged across weeks

rules.title: Federal — EAP Exemption Salary Level $684/week (29 CFR 541.600)

result.summary: An executive, administrative or professional employee is exempt from FLSA overtime only if paid on a salary basis at least $684 a week ($35,568 a year), plus $107,432 total annual compensation for the highly compensated employee test. The 2024 rule raising these levels was vacated (E.D. Tex. 2024-11-15) and formally rescinded by DOL on 2026-05-15, so the 2019 levels remain in force. States may set higher thresholds.

rules.title: New York — Exempt Salary Threshold $1,275/week in NYC, Long Island and Westchester, 2026

params.basis: 12 NYCRR 142-2.14 schedule; about 75 x minimum wage

result.summary: Executive and administrative employees in New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester counties are exempt from state overtime only if paid at least $1,275.00 a week ($66,300 a year) in 2026. New York sets no salary minimum for the professional exemption, so the federal $684 applies there.

citations.source: 12 NYCRR §142-2.14 (Exemptions) and Minimum Wage Order schedules

rules.title: New York Call-In Pay — On-Call Employee (minimum 4 hours)

rules.title: New York Split Shift / Spread-of-Hours Premium (extra hour at min wage)

result.summary: 1 additional hour at basic minimum hourly wage when interval between start and end of workday exceeds 10 hours. Applies to all industries covered by NY wage orders.

rules.title: New York Spread of Hours Pay (>10 hr span = +1 hr at min wage)

result.summary: 1 additional hour at the applicable minimum wage rate

rules.title: New York — Weekly Pay for Manual Workers

params.applies_to: Manual workers (over 25% physical labor); job category used as a proxy
params.notes: Semimonthly only with Commissioner authorization under §191(1)(a)(ii); liquidated damages litigation under §198 is common

result.summary: Manual workers must be paid weekly, within 7 days after the week's work, unless the employer holds a Commissioner authorization to pay semimonthly (available only to employers of 1,000 or more).

rules.title: New York — Pay Frequency

params.notes: Manual workers weekly (see ny-pay-frequency-manual-workers); railroad workers by Thursday for the prior week

result.summary: Clerical and other workers must be paid at least semimonthly on regular paydays designated in advance; commissioned salespersons at least monthly.

rules.title: FLSA — Wage Deductions

result.summary: Under the FLSA, deductions for items that primarily benefit the employer (uniforms, tools, cash shortages, damage) may not reduce pay below the minimum wage or cut into overtime.

citations.source: 29 CFR §531.35 (wages must be paid free and clear)
US DOL Fact Sheet #16: Deductions from Wages for Uniforms and Other Facilities

rules.title: New York — Wage Deductions

params.penalty: liquidated damages of 100% of wages due
params.notes: Overpayment and advance recoveries only under 12 NYCRR 195; expanded §193 sunsets 2028-11-06

result.summary: Deductions are limited to those required by law and voluntary, revocable, written authorizations for the employee's benefit on the statute's list; shortages, breakage, damage and fines may never be deducted.

citations.source: Ezel, Employee Wage Deduction Requirements by State (survey)

rules.title: Equal Pay Act of 1963 — Equal Pay

params.notes: Covers all FLSA-covered employers; NLRA §7 separately protects most non-supervisory employees who discuss wages

result.summary: Employees of the opposite sex doing equal work (equal skill, effort and responsibility under similar conditions) in the same establishment must be paid equally unless a seniority, merit, production or other factor-other-than-sex system explains the gap.

rules.title: New York — Equal Pay

params.protected_classes: all protected classes under Executive Law §296
params.notes: Substantially similar standard since 2016-01-19; all protected classes since 2019-10-08; liquidated damages up to 300%

result.summary: Employees in a protected class may not be paid less for equal work or substantially similar work (viewed as a composite of skill, effort and responsibility under similar conditions) unless a seniority, merit, production or bona fide factor other than status explains the whole gap; wage discussion may not be prohibited.

citations.source: Paycor, Pay Equity and State-by-State Laws (survey)

rules.title: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act: anti-discrimination coverage

params.protected_classes: race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity per Bostock), national origin

result.summary: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act applies to employers with 15+ employees and prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity per Bostock), national origin.

rules.title: Americans with Disabilities Act, Title I: anti-discrimination coverage

params.protected_classes: disability; reasonable accommodation required absent undue hardship

result.summary: Americans with Disabilities Act, Title I applies to employers with 15+ employees and prohibits discrimination based on disability; reasonable accommodation required absent undue hardship.

rules.title: Age Discrimination in Employment Act: anti-discrimination coverage

result.summary: Age Discrimination in Employment Act applies to employers with 20+ employees and prohibits discrimination based on age 40 and over.

rules.title: Pregnant Workers Fairness Act: anti-discrimination coverage

params.protected_classes: known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth or related conditions; reasonable accommodation required

result.summary: Pregnant Workers Fairness Act applies to employers with 15+ employees and prohibits discrimination based on known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth or related conditions; reasonable accommodation required.

rules.title: Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act, Title II: anti-discrimination coverage

params.protected_classes: genetic information, including family medical history

result.summary: Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act, Title II applies to employers with 15+ employees and prohibits discrimination based on genetic information, including family medical history.

rules.title: Civil Rights Act of 1866 (Section 1981): anti-discrimination coverage

params.protected_classes: race and ethnicity in making and enforcing contracts, including employment; no employer-size floor

result.summary: Civil Rights Act of 1866 (Section 1981) applies to employers of any size and prohibits discrimination based on race and ethnicity in making and enforcing contracts, including employment; no employer-size floor.

rules.title: USERRA anti-discrimination: anti-discrimination coverage

params.protected_classes: past, present or future uniformed service membership or obligations

result.summary: USERRA anti-discrimination applies to employers of any size and prohibits discrimination based on past, present or future uniformed service membership or obligations.

rules.title: New York: state anti-discrimination law coverage

params.protected_classes: federal classes plus those in notes
params.notes: Also covers military status, predisposing genetic characteristics, familial status, domestic violence victim status, reproductive health decisions, citizenship or immigration status; age 18+.

result.summary: New York's fair employment law covers employers of any size; sexual orientation is and gender identity is expressly protected. Also covers military status, predisposing genetic characteristics, familial status, domestic violence victim status, reproductive health decisions, citizenship or immigration status; age 18+.

citations.source: Workplace Fairness, Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity Discrimination: State Law

rules.title: New York: annual sexual harassment prevention training (all employers)

params.notes: Interactive; must meet or exceed the state model training. Covers anyone working any portion of time in New York.

result.summary: Every New York employer must give all employees interactive sexual harassment prevention training every year.

citations.source: Ethena, Harassment Training Requirements by City and State (2026)

rules.title: New York City: annual sexual harassment training (15+ employees)

params.notes: Independent contractors count toward the threshold; covers employees and interns working 80+ hours a year and 90+ days. Records kept 3 years.

result.summary: New York City employers with 15+ employees (including independent contractors) must give annual interactive sexual harassment training.

citations.source: Ethena, Harassment Training Requirements by City and State (2026)

rules.title: New York: written sexual harassment prevention policy (all employers)

params.distribution: in writing or electronically to all employees, in English and the employee's primary language where a state model exists
params.notes: Adopt the state model policy or one meeting its minimums, including a complaint form.

result.summary: Every New York employer must adopt and distribute a written sexual harassment prevention policy meeting the state model.

citations.source: ADP, Which States Require a Written Harassment Prevention Policy

rules.title: Federal OSHA: coverage and general duty clause

params.agency: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
params.notes: Covers private employers in all states; the general duty clause requires a workplace free of recognized serious hazards. States with approved plans enforce their own standards (see state rules).

result.summary: Private employers are covered by the OSH Act and must keep the workplace free of recognized hazards likely to cause death or serious harm.

rules.title: Federal OSHA: injury and illness recordkeeping (11+ employees)

params.forms: OSHA 300 log, 301 incident reports, 300A annual summary posted Feb 1 to Apr 30
params.exemptions: Establishments in partially exempt low-hazard industries (Appendix A to Subpart B) need not keep the log; all employers must report fatalities within 8 hours and in-patient hospitalizations, amputations or eye losses within 24 hours.
params.electronic_submission: Establishments with 20-249 employees in designated industries and 250+ employees submit 300A electronically; 100+ in designated industries also submit 300/301 data (since 2024).

result.summary: Employers with 11+ employees (outside partially exempt industries) must keep OSHA 300 logs and post the 300A summary; every employer must report severe injuries.

rules.title: New York: workplace safety enforcement authority

params.agency: Federal OSHA (state plan covers public employees only)
params.notes: Federal standards (29 C.F.R. Parts 1904, 1910, 1926) apply.

result.summary: New York's State Plan covers only state and local government workers; private employers remain under federal OSHA.

citations.source: OSHA, State Plans: Frequently Asked Questions

rules.title: New York: Retail Worker Safety Act policy and training (10+ retail employees)

params.training: at hire and annually (every 2 years for employers with fewer than 50 retail employees)
params.notes: Adopt the Department of Labor model policy or an equivalent; training covers de-escalation, active shooter, emergency procedures and emergency devices. Retail store means one selling consumer commodities and not primarily food for on-premises consumption.

result.summary: New York retail employers with 10+ retail employees must adopt a workplace violence prevention policy and train workers at hire and periodically.

citations.source: Poster Compliance Center, Workplace Violence Laws: California and New York

rules.title: New York: silent response buttons for large retailers (500+ retail employees)

params.notes: Employers with 500+ retail employees nationwide must provide silent response buttons (fixed or wearable) that summon security or management.

result.summary: From 2027 New York retailers with 500+ retail employees nationwide must provide silent response (panic) buttons.

citations.source: Poster Compliance Center, Workplace Violence Laws: California and New York

rules.title: OSH Act § 11(c): retaliation for safety complaints prohibited

params.protected_activity: filing a safety or health complaint, participating in an inspection, refusing imminently dangerous work
params.notes: Complaints go to OSHA within 30 days; no private right of action.

result.summary: Employers may not discharge or discriminate against an employee for raising safety concerns or exercising OSH Act rights.

rules.title: FLSA § 15(a)(3): retaliation for wage complaints prohibited

params.protected_activity: filing a wage-hour complaint, oral or written, internal or to the Department of Labor; testifying in an FLSA proceeding
params.notes: Private right of action with back pay, liquidated damages and reinstatement.

result.summary: Employers may not retaliate against an employee for complaining about minimum wage or overtime violations.

rules.title: Title VII § 704(a): retaliation for opposing discrimination prohibited

params.protected_activity: opposing unlawful discrimination or participating in an EEOC charge, investigation or proceeding
params.notes: Parallel provisions in the ADA (42 U.S.C. § 12203), ADEA (29 U.S.C. § 623(d)) and PWFA.

result.summary: Employers with 15+ employees may not retaliate against employees who oppose discrimination or take part in EEOC proceedings.

rules.title: NLRA § 7: protected concerted activity

params.protected_activity: employees acting together about wages, hours or working conditions, including discussing pay and raising group complaints, union or not
params.notes: Covers most private employers meeting NLRB jurisdictional thresholds; excludes supervisors, agricultural workers and independent contractors.

result.summary: Private employers may not discipline or restrain employees for concerted activity about working conditions, including discussing pay.

rules.title: New York: whistleblower protection for private employees

params.notes: As amended 2022, protects disclosure or threatened disclosure of activity the employee reasonably believes violates law or poses a substantial danger to public health or safety; covers former employees and independent contractors; posting required.

result.summary: New York has a general whistleblower statute covering private employers. As amended 2022, protects disclosure or threatened disclosure of activity the employee reasonably believes violates law or poses a substantial danger to public health or safety; covers former employees and independent contractors; posting required.

citations.source: Tate & Renner, State Whistleblower Law Chart

rules.title: New York Additional Evening Meal Break (shift past 7pm)

result.summary: 20-minute meal break for shifts of 10+ hours

rules.title: New York Meal Break — Non-Factory (>6 hr shift spanning noon)

result.summary: 30-minute meal break for shifts of 6+ hours

rules.title: New York — Meal Break Required (shifts > 6 hrs)

result.summary: New York requires a 30-minute meal break for shifts over 6 hours. Ensure a break is scheduled.

rules.title: New York — No Waiver; One Employee on Duty May Eat on the Job With Voluntary Consent (Labor Law §162)

result.summary: Meal periods under Labor Law §162 cannot be waived. Where only one person is on duty or is the only one in a specific occupation, the employee may eat on the job without being relieved, but only with the employee's voluntary consent, and an employee who asks for an uninterrupted meal must get one. Shorter periods (not less than 20 minutes) require a written, posted permit from the Commissioner (LS 443 guidelines). In force before 2000.

citations.source: N.Y. Labor Law §162 (Time allowed for meals)
NYS DOL, LS 443 Guidelines for Meal Periods

rules.title: NYC Retail — 72-Hour Advance Notice Required

result.summary: Posting retail employee schedules with less than 72 hours advance notice

citations.source: NYC Admin Code §20-1251 (Fair Workweek Law, retail)

rules.title: NYC retail — No Added Shifts With <72 Hours Notice Without Written Consent

result.summary: A retail employer may not add a shift or hours with less than 72 hours notice unless the employee consents in writing

rules.title: NYC retail — No Cancelling Shifts With <72 Hours Notice

result.summary: A retail employer may not cancel, shorten or move a shift with less than 72 hours notice (except for emergencies, or when the employee asks)

rules.title: NYC Retail — On-Call Scheduling Prohibited

result.summary: Requiring retail employees to be on-call (must schedule or not schedule; cannot require availability without pay)

citations.source: NYC Admin Code §20-1252 (Fair Workweek Law, retail)

rules.title: New York City — Temporary Schedule Change Law: Two Changes a Year for Personal Events

result.summary: Any employee who has worked 120 days and 80 or more hours a year in the city may make two temporary schedule changes per calendar year (each up to one business day, or one of two days) for a personal event: caring for a minor child or a care recipient, a legal proceeding for public benefits, or any reason covered by Paid Safe and Sick Leave. The employer must respond immediately, may propose unpaid leave instead of the requested change, and must answer a written request in writing within 14 days stating the decision and remaining changes. Employees may also request other changes, which the employer may deny but not retaliate against. Excludes government, certain CBA-covered and entertainment employees.

citations.source: NYC Administrative Code §§20-1261–20-1263 (Temporary Changes to Work Schedules)
NYC DCWP, Temporary Schedule Change Law overview

rules.title: Federal Lactation Break Time (PUMP Act)

result.summary: Reasonable break time each time the employee needs to express milk for one year after the child's birth, in a private non-bathroom space; unpaid unless the employee is not fully relieved or uses a paid break (employers under 50 may claim undue hardship)
